units.translation: 71. περαιόθεν: it is formed from πέρας and περαία and περαιόθεν. Hence all land is called ἤπειρος by catachresis, but properly it is that which extends to infinity, as Euripides has made clear (fr. 1010 N.²): ‘ἤπειρον εἰς ἄπειρον ἐκβάλλων χθόνα.’
19 Apoll. Lex. Hom. 84, 20 B. Hesych. ἤπειρος Συν. ἡ. (251, 20 Ba. Phot. Suid.) Io. Philop. Comm. in Arist. Meteor. 19, 23 Hayd. Or. Werf 613, 55 Et. M. 433, 54 Et. Gud. 246, 59 Sturz
18 πέρας καὶ περαία in K : περαία καὶ πέρας in L : differently in P
22 ἤπειρον in P : ἄπ- in L ἐκβάλλων in L : ἐσβάλλω in P
86. φεύγωμεν, πρὶν τόνδε θοῶν: Apollonius says that Medea fled to the ship at night, while Aeetes was holding a council
23 τόνδε in F : τῶνδε in L : omitted in P

of the Colchians about the destruction of the heroes; but the author of the Naupactica (fr. 8 Kink.) says that Aeetes was put to sleep by Aphrodite, because he desired to have intercourse with his own wife, after the Argonauts had dined at his house and were sleeping, because he wanted to burn the ship;
but Idmon understood what had happened and says:
and Medea, hearing the sound of footsteps, rose up and rushed out with them. Herodorus (31 fr. 53 J.) also says these things.
4 Ἀργοναυτῶν in K : Κόλχων
11 φευγέμεν ἐκ Meineke : φευγέμεναι

87. δώσω δὲ χρύσειον: Apollonius has Medea, after fleeing from Aeetes' house, promising the fleece to Jason; but the author of the Naupactica (fr. 9 Kink.) has her carrying out the fleece with her during her flight, it being kept in his own house [of Aeetes]; but Herodorus (31 fr. 52 J.) says that after the yoking of the wild bulls Jason was sent by Aeetes for the fleece, and that he went and killed the dragon and brought the fleece to Aeetes, and that he treacherously invited them to dinner.
17 αὑτοῦ in L : omitted in PA, deleted by W
18 ἀγρίων ταύρων C. Mueller : Ἀργοναυτῶν
89. ἐπίιστορας: witnesses. LgP
91. ὀνοτήν: blameworthy. LgP
94. προσπτύξατο: embraced. LgP
102. παρέκ νόον Αἰήταο: against the will of Aeetes. Lg (P)
104. 〈ἔωσαν:〉 they drove. Lg
106. ἔμπαλιν ἀίσσουσα: rushing backwards. LgP
111 a. ἄγχαυρον: the time near and close to daybreak.
28 Et. Gen. (B) ἄγχαυρον: the so-called twilight. It signifies the early morning time, near the breeze, that is, the day; ἀγχίαυρος and ἄγχαυρος.
28 τὸν καιρὸν τὸν πλησίον τῆς ἡμέρας Sm
like twilight; for at such a time the breezes blow. This is from the poet (ε 469): ‘αὔρη δ’ ἐκ ποταμοῦ ψυχρὴ πέλει ἠῶθι πρό.’
1 λυκόφως W : λυκόφωτα in L : τὸ καλούμενον λυκόφως in P περὶ — πνέουσι in P : omitted in L
7 deleted by W
[αὖρα δὲ ἡ ἡμέρα deleted by W]. Thus I found in the scholia on the Argonautica of Apollonius. cf. W 70
b. κνώσσουσιν: they are drowsy. Lg (P)
